Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. in_hebrew.name: סטפניה
in_hebrew.meaning: עטרת או כתר של אלוהים, משמעות רוחנית עמוקה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם סטפניה נגזר מהמילה היוונית סטפאנוס, שפירושה כתר. בהקשר הנוצרי, השם מייצג את הכתר הרוחני שמקבלים המאמינים המשרתים את אלוהים. השם משויך לאחד הנוצרים הראשונים, סטפנוס, שהיה אחד משבעה דיאקונים שנבחרו על ידי השליחים כדי לשרת את הקהילה הנוצרית הראשונה בירושלים.

in_greek.name: Στεφανία
in_greek.meaning: Στεφανία, το στέφανος του Θεού, πνευματική έννοια
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Στεφανία προέρχεται από το ελληνικό στέφανος, που σημαίνει κορόνη ή στεφάνι. Στον χριστιανικό περίγραμμα, το όνομα αντιπροσωπεύει το πνευματικό στεφάνι που λαμβάνουν οι πιστοί που υπηρετούν τον Θεό. Σχετίζεται με τον πρώτο χριστιανό μάρτυρα, τον Στέφανο, που ήταν ένας από τους επτά διακόνους που εκλέχθηκαν από τους αποστόλους για να υπηρετήσουν την πρώτη χριστιανική κοινότητα στην Ιερουσαλήμ.

in_latin.name: Stephania
in_latin.meaning: Crown of God, spiritual significance deeply rooted
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Stephania derives from the Greek word Stephanos, meaning crown. In Christian context, it represents the spiritual crown received by believers serving God. Associated with Stephen, one of the first Christians and a deacon in the early Christian church in Jerusalem, known for his martyrdom.

in_english.name: Stefania
in_english.meaning: Crown of God, symbolizing spiritual victory and honor
in_english.long_meaning: The name Stefania originates from the Greek word 'Stephanos,' meaning 'crown.' It carries a rich spiritual significance in Christian tradition, symbolizing the crown of martyrdom and honor bestowed upon believers who serve God faithfully. Historically, the name is linked to Saint Stephen, one of the first deacons of the Christian church, known for his faith and martyrdom. The name Stefania reflects virtues of spiritual strength, devotion, and the pursuit of divine reward.

The name continues to be used today, and its popularity can be seen in various art forms and mass media.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, the name Stefania holds a deep spiritual significance representing devotion, loyalty, and spiritual growth. The name is reminiscent of Saint Stefania, a symbol of trust and faith in God, and her enduring legacy inspires those bearing the name to follow in her footsteps. The name Stefania is also associated with the idea of being crowned with honor and grace in the eyes of the Lord, emphasizing the spiritual achievements and rewards earned through a faithful and dedicated life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Stefania symbolizes the pure and steadfast devotion to God, represented by the name's Greek origin - "Crown of God." It embodies the strength and constancy in faith, much like the unwavering faith of St. Stefanos and St. Stephanos.

historical_references.reference: There is a medieval saint named Saint Stefanija, also known as Saint Stefana, who was believed to have lived in the 11th century in Dalmatia, Croatia. She is the patron saint of Dalmatia, and is venerated as the queen of the sea and the protector of sailors. According to legend, she was a wealthy noblewoman who dedicated her life to helping the poor and the sick. One day, she was approached by pirates who demanded that she give them her wealth. Instead of complying, she gave them her jewels and her servants, but kept her faith in God. The pirates, impressed by her piety, released her and her servants. From that day on, she devoted her life to helping the poor and the sick, and was eventually canonized.

Another Saint Stefania is Saint Stefania of Rome, who lived in the 4th century. She was a wealthy Roman woman who was converted to Christianity by Pope Sylvester I. She dedicated her life to charitable works and helping the poor, and was known for her generosity and her devotion to the faith. She was eventually martyred during the Diocletian persecutions, and her relics were later interred in the Basilica of San Stefano Rotondo in Rome.
